Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The bug report states that when dealing with nested groups of options (Group A as a child of Group B) with minimum and maximum constraints set on the parent group (Group B), the presence of the child group does not affect the parent group as expected. This occurs because groups themselves are never added to the CommandLine instance, so CommandLine.hasOption(A) will always return false for a group A, and it isn't counted towards the constraints.

Looking in the implementation of WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option), we see that it only adds the option itself (adds to an internal options collection and maps its triggers), but there is no handling of the option's children or nested groups. This method does not propagate presence information up the group hierarchy.

Similarly, WriteableCommandLineImpl.hasOption(Option) only checks if the option is directly present in the options collection, so nested group presence is not counted.

The failure to propagate presence information for nested groups means constraints on parent groups do not account for their children option groups properly, causing the reported issue.

Therefore, the problem occurs because WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option) and corresponding presence tracking fail to mark a group as present if any of its children options/groups are present. Consequently, hasOption does not reflect nested group presence, resulting in incorrect evaluation of min/max constraints.

Fixing this would require changing addOption so that if option is a group, or it contains children, the group itself is also added to indicate its presence, thus enabling hasOption and constraint checks to work correctly with nested groups.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
